reading.body:
At 9 MW, CyrusOne's SAT1 campus in San Antonio is a mid-size facility by AI standards, and it is one of only 19 Texas data centers that publish a power figure at all.

Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities, but just 19 disclose IT load. The 475 MW state total is therefore a sum over a small voluntary subset, not a measurement of the state's actual load. SAT1 contributes 9 MW of that, or 1.9%, ranking 14th in published capacity statewide. Any claim about Texas data center power, including its standing behind California and Virginia, rests on that same thin disclosure base and should be read as a floor rather than a total.

For AI specifically, 9 MW and 110,000 square feet of technical space is a regulated-workload facility, not a training site. The certifications listed, HIPAA, PCI DSS, FISMA, ISO 27001, SSAE 16 Type II, TIA-942, point to financial services and government-sensitive compute. The roughly 225 racks figure comes from applying an assumed 40 kW per rack to the published capacity, so it describes a possible configuration rather than anything the operator states. The suitability score of 56 is built from published IT capacity and operator type alone, with announced expansion listed as missing.

What the data does not cover is as important as what it does. There is no backup power capacity, no renewable sourcing, no grid interconnection detail, no address, and no nearest airport. Those omissions are the ones that would matter most for judging whether this site can actually be powered at scale, and they are not disclosed by the operator.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
